content.comment_body: Hello, is it possible to store an analog value to an SD card and retrieve it when required? I want to use this option to restore the program from a saved analog value in case of power loss or manual interruption. If anyone can share examples, I would appreciate it.

With the [product_name] program, you can't read a value directly from the SD card; you can only write it into a Data Log stored there. However, you can save values in a fail-safe manner using standard program features, allowing you to reuse these values when restarting after a power outage. Could you elaborate on your intended approach?

I've designed an aquarium light scheduling routine, thanks to the input from this forum. It uses a counter and ramp functions to create a specific analog value at one output. Ideally, I'd like to save this output value and use it as the starting point for the counter after a restart. For instance, if the output is 700 and the power goes off and on again, the program should resume from 700. Usually, if the power fails during ramp-up, the program would revert to zero.
Can you provide more details or examples about saving values in a voltage fail-safe manner within the program for reuse on restart?
Can someone clarify what it means to save values (like analog outputs) in a voltage fail-safe way using the program, so they can be accessed after restarting the device?

Hello, [user_name]. Check your diagram—if blocks 8 and 9 have the Retentivity function enabled, it will help. Also, refer to the attached image file; you can get more information by searching for 'retentivity' in the help system.
Thank you, [user_name]. It's straightforward yet very useful!

analysis.insight_summary: A user aims to retain an analog value through power interruptions by saving it to an SD card and restoring it upon restart. It was clarified that direct retrieval from SD card isn't supported, and only data logging to the card is possible. Users are directed to utilize retentivity functions for fail-safe analog data persistence, indicating an ongoing learning process for managing persistent values in automation programs.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to reliably save an analog value within the program so that the device automatically restores and continues from this value after a power outage, maintaining uninterrupted automated scheduling.
